question: The action of chlorine on dry Ca(OH)₂, produces which of the following?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bleaching powder**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The reaction of **dry chlorine gas** with **calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂)** leads to the formation of **bleaching powder**.
 
• The chemical formula of bleaching powder is **Ca(OCl)₂** (Calcium Oxychloride).
 
• The reaction occurs as follows:

 **Cl₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → Ca(OCl)₂ + H₂O**
 
• **Bleaching powder** is widely used as a **disinfectant** and a **bleaching agent**.
 
• It is particularly effective for **water purification** and as a **fungicide** in agriculture.
 
• Bleaching powder is also used in the **textile industry** for bleaching fabrics and in the **paper industry** for bleaching wood pulp.
 
• This compound is a good source of **chlorine** and releases chlorine when it comes into contact with water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid**__

 __
 
• **Hydrochloric acid (HCl)** is a strong acid formed when hydrogen chloride is dissolved in water.
 
• It is mainly used in the **chemical industry** for large-scale production of organic compounds such as vinyl chloride and dichloroethane.
 
• It is also used in the **food industry** for processing food products and in cleaning applications.
 
• Hydrochloric acid is not formed during the reaction of dry chlorine with Ca(OH)₂.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Chloride**__
 __
 
• **Calcium chloride (CaCl₂)** is a highly soluble salt used for **de-icing roads** and as a **desiccant** in drying processes.
 
• It is also used in the **food industry** as a firming agent and in **construction** to accelerate the setting of concrete.
 
• Although calcium chloride can be formed in some chemical reactions involving chlorine, it is not the product of the reaction between dry chlorine and Ca(OH)₂.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Oxide**__
 
 
• **Calcium oxide (CaO)**, also known as **quicklime**, is a widely used chemical compound in the **steel, paper, and chemical industries**.
 
• It is obtained by heating limestone (CaCO₃) and does not result from the reaction of chlorine with Ca(OH)₂.
 
• Calcium oxide is known for its use in **neutralizing acidic soils** in agriculture.
